title: Moon Bricks

museumIntro: Move the paddle with the arrow keys and keep the ball bouncing until every brick disappears. Where the ball meets the paddle changes its direction. Try a wider paddle for an easier game or a faster ball for a challenge.

museumStory.title: 1976: Breakout and the brick breaker
museumStory.text:
An early landmark for brick-breaking games was Atari’s Breakout, released in 1976. It took the paddle-and-ball idea of Pong and made a solo challenge: knock down a wall of bricks. The arcade machine used a black-and-white screen with a coloured overlay to give the rows their colours.

Moon Bricks is our version of this game type. The paddle, ball and wall give you a small set of rules to understand, then change.
museumStory.prompt: What if the paddle were twice as wide? Would every bounce become easier to aim?
